title: Add headless SSR RAG quickstart with devcontainer and browser debug proxy
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a minimal headless SSR RAG quickstart with devcontainer, two example runtimes (Node/Edge), and a lightweight browser debug proxy for streaming inspection.
description:
Summary: Introduces a headless SSR Rapid Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) quickstart that demonstrates how to integrate Redwood hosted inference into server-side rendering flows. The intent is to give frontend and platform engineers a small, reproducible starter that: 1) runs in a devcontainer, 2) supports headless/server-side streaming for SSR responses, and 3) includes an optional lightweight browser debug proxy to inspect streaming events and KV cache behavior without changing production code.

Motivation and context: Teams building product features that render LLM responses server-side face subtle problems around streaming, tokenization differences between client and server, and debugging tools. Existing quickstarts cover in-browser RAG and agent tool-calling, but we lacked a concise example for headless SSR (Next-style, edge and node). This PR adds a minimal pattern to avoid anti-patterns we've seen in support cases (SUP-843) and provides guidance for safe timeouts, CSP headers, and caching semantics.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds /templates/headless-ssr which contains a minimal Next-like server-rendering example (server-only route, streaming SSE and polyfilled fetch).
- Adds a devcontainer configuration (.devcontainer/) with lightweight GPU passthrough notes and reproducible tooling for local testing.
- Provides two runtime variants: node-express (standard) and edge-min (Deno/edge-compatible) with matching README docs and env examples.
- Adds a small browser debug proxy (tools/ssr-stream-proxy) that can optionally be mounted during development to open a websocket/UI for inspecting partial responses, KV cache hits, and latency traces. The proxy is intentionally small and opt-in (commented in the devcontainer).
- Adds docs/quickstarts/headless-ssr.md with best-practices, CSP suggestions, recommended Redwood SDK settings (batching=false for first token, streaming=true, kv_cache=prefix), and a checklist for production rollout.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Example server route and server-render template
- [x] Devcontainer and run instructions
- [x] Edge-compatible runtime example
- [x] Browser debug proxy and short guide
- [x] README and quickstart doc
- [x] Automated integration test for SSR endpoint (basic smoke test)

Commits (summary):
- Initial scaffold of templates/headless-ssr with Node and Edge examples
- Add .devcontainer and README with step-by-step runbook
- Implement tools/ssr-stream-proxy and lightweight UI for inspection
- Add docs/quickstarts/headless-ssr.md and internal checklist
- Fix lint/ESM import ordering and add CI workflow for quickstart smoke tests

Files changed (high-level):
- templates/headless-ssr/ (server.tsx, sse-handler.ts, edge-handler.ts, example-fetch.ts)
- tools/ssr-stream-proxy/ (proxy.js, ui.html, README.md)
- .devcontainer/devcontainer.json, .devcontainer/Dockerfile.dev
- docs/quickstarts/headless-ssr.md
- .github/workflows/quickstarts-smoke.yml (added a matrix job to validate Node/Edge smoke tests)
- tests/quickstarts/headless-ssr.test.ts (basic response streaming assertions)

Notes on security and production readiness: The proxy is explicitly disabled in the production README. The docs call out CSP header guidance and recommend setting the dev-only proxy behind an auth guard if used in shared environments. I added a short security checklist in the docs to ensure teams consider KMS for keys and HSTS/CSP when exposing endpoints.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Marco Liang (review): "Nice concise pattern — can we ensure server SSE closes correctly on client disconnect and that we don't buffer the entire response?"
  - Aisha: "Addressed in sse-handler: we now use response.flush() with a short keepalive and explicit abort on request 'close' event. Added test to assert no full-body buffering."
- Sofia Reyes (review): "Please add CSP examples and a note about X-Accel-Buffering in nginx fronting SSR endpoints. Also, the devcontainer Dockerfile had an unpinned base image."
  - Aisha: "Added CSP snippet in docs, mention of X-Accel-Buffering, and switched to pinned node:lts-slim@sha256 in the devcontainer Dockerfile."
- Luis Ortega (review): "CI failed once due to ESM import ordering; please run repo linting."
  - Aisha: "Fixed import order and added an ESLint override for the quickstarts folder. CI reran and passed."

CI summary: The new workflow quickstarts-smoke.yml runs a matrix for node/edge and includes lint/static checks and the smoke test. First run: lint failed (ESM imports). Second run: all checks passed. Final CI status: pass.

Testing: Added tests/quickstarts/headless-ssr.test.ts that starts the example server in a child process, establishes an SSE connection, and validates incremental chunks and final json metadata. The test is lightweight and runs in ~6s on CI.

Docs and examples: The README contains a minimal API key example and a short troubleshooting section with answers to common SSR pitfalls: 1) tokenization mismatches between client and server, 2) KV cache prefixing to avoid cross-route pollution, 3) recommended timeout values for server-side calls.

Backward compatibility and breaking changes: None. The quickstart is additive and opt-in. The only repo change that could affect other flows is the addition of an ESLint override file under .eslintrc.quickstarts.json; it is scoped and documented.

Merge: After two approvals (Marco, Sofia) and green CI, merged via squash to main on 2026-03-04.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add an optional example that demonstrates server-side tool-calling with safe sandboxed execution (future PR).
- Add a short video walkthrough for the devcontainer flow and debugging proxy.

Related work and references: Linked Linear items ENG-2239 (headless-ssr quickstart epic), PM-118 (doc rollout), and support ticket SUP-843 with repro notes.

If you want to run this locally: clone the repo, cd templates/headless-ssr, cp .env.example .env (set REDWOOD_API_KEY), and:
  - docker compose up (devcontainer: open in container)
  - npm install && npm run dev:node (or npm run dev:edge)
  - optional: cd tools/ssr-stream-proxy && node proxy.js then open http://localhost:8080/ui to watch streaming frames.

This PR aims to be a compact, low-maintenance example teams can fork or reference when migrating server-side LLM rendering to Redwood.
